verdicts.why: A scientific law names a regularity in nature and takes no side on it.
'The law' for the police is informal in register but carries no approval or contempt beyond naming the force.
Natural or moral law as a body of binding rules is described, not judged, by the word.
The name of a branch of philosophy or study is a plain label.
A single room or single bed is meant for one; the word states capacity without attitude.
A single purpose or single aim is undivided; that is the meaning, not a judgement of it.
A single rule applying uniformly to all is a plain description of scope.
A botanical term for petal arrangement judges nothing.
Refusing to accept a claim as true is a plain act; the word neither sides with nor against the denier.
Refusing to acknowledge someone or something may be an ugly act, but the ugliness sits in the referent, not in the word, which is plainer than 'disown'.
Denying oneself a pleasure is described neutrally; the word carries neither praise for restraint nor pity for it.
A formal legal denial of an allegation is a technical term with no attitude attached.
The act of blending things so their distinctions are lost names a disorder plainly; any unpleasantness belongs to the referent.
To perform a duty or task is a somewhat formal way of saying 'do', with no judgement of the doer or the deed.
In the sense of causing something to occur (provoke laughter, provoke a reaction) the word is a plain causative and the 'annoy' sense is a different synset.
A recognized right or entitlement, as in a claim to the throne, is stated without the speaker taking a side on it.
A claim in the sense of a demand made on someone is a neutral label for the demand itself.
A ship going under is a plain physical event and the word adds no attitude to it.
Falling to a lower level, whether physically or in someone's esteem, is described rather than judged; the loss is the referent, not the word.
Sinking into a chair or into silence is a neutral image of descent into something enveloping.
Falling or dropping heavily is a manner of movement, not an attitude toward whoever falls.
The sun appearing to sink is pure description.
Embedding a post or a shaft deeply is a technical, attitude-free use.
Being rightly placed in a class or category is classification, not evaluation.
Being suitable or in its proper place is the word's meaning; a speaker saying something does not belong is judging through the meaning, not through any extra colouring of the word.
